key_insight: RRSI argues that agent self-improvement should be treated as a controlled optimization problem, not an unconstrained loop of edits. By regularizing recursive changes to the agent harness, it aims to improve performance while reducing overfitting to the training tasks.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the instability and overfitting that can arise when LLM agents repeatedly rewrite their own harnesses—prompts, control flow, tools, memory, and context management—to improve task performance.
method: Treat the agent harness as the target of recursive self-improvement, with iterative proposals and selection of component-level edits.
Add regularization to constrain harness evolution and reduce memorization of training tasks.
Evaluate whether the improved harness transfers better beyond the tasks used to optimize it.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical way to make agent systems more robust, generalizable, and easier to optimize safely. It is especially relevant for building autonomous agents that adapt without drifting into brittle or task-specific hacks.
visual_elements: Before/after pipeline diagram showing a frozen backbone model wrapped by an evolving harness
Recursive loop graphic with propose → select → regularize → evaluate steps
Chart comparing training-task performance vs. generalization performance

paper_title: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
paper_authors: Peng Xia, Rujun Han, Zifeng Wang, Yanfei Chen, Yufan Zhang
